items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Tracey Hare and Ian McLean, Immigration Partnership Council
notes:
T. Hare and I. McLean provided information related to the works of the Immigration Partnership. They expressed concern that the federal government decreased their funding by 30% when the need to support newcomers is at an all-time high. They requested $175,000 in funding assistance. 

In response to the Committee, I. McLean explained that the federal government decreased their funding to level the funding across all areas, however, this severely impacts the Immigration Partnership because their programming is more extensive. Tara Bedard, Executive Director Immigration Partnership, further explained that the programming is interconnected and includes statistical reporting to determine the primary needs of the community through data analysis. The level of analysis required is not possible with the decrease in funding.

C. James expressed support for the requested funding as well as advocating to the federal government about restoring the government funding to previous levels.

items.title: CSD-HOU-25-009, The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness – Progress Update
notes:
Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, introduced the report and staff. Jennifer Gordon, Manager Homelessness & Supportive Housing, and Chris McEvoy, Manager Homelessness & Supportive Housing, provided a presentation to update the Committee on the progress of the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness (PECH). A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. The team reported that 70% of the 30 identified actions under the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness (PECH) are currently being advanced. This plan is designed to work with Building Better Futures and the Housing Revitalization Project to span the entire housing continuum. The All of Community Approach was launched, formalizing the PECH Leadership Table and co-creators group. Christine Allison from Engage Rural Collaborative highlighted the importance of embedding rural realities in policy. She cited the example of the inclement weather fund and the provision of flexible rent supplements distributed directly by rural agencies to prevent eviction, reflecting a broader system shift.

The update highlights the collaborative, place-based, and equity-focused approach of PECH, emphasizing its goal of achieving functional zero homelessness across the region. Speakers from co-creator groups detailed how the initiative is fostering system change, particularly through prevention and data-driven equity work.
Marjorie Knight, Rhythm and Blues Cambridge, compared the effort to turning a "big ship," noting that PECH brought together people from various organizations who previously had little interaction. She highlighted the success of the PECH rent supplement to prevent them from falling into homelessness. She described the use of funds for a needs assessment study to gather missing data on diverse populations, ensuring more effective and equitable decision-making.

Dr. Fadhilah Balogun, African Women's Alliance of Waterloo Region, acknowledged Council's investments and explained how these initiatives empowered her organization to actively participate in prevention among newcomer and racialized families often overlooked by mainstream strategies. The collaboration helped include "invisible forms" of housing instability that disproportionately affect newcomers, such as overcrowding, hidden homelessness, and precarious living situations. She emphasized that supporting community-led and culturally grounded organizations achieves equitable and sustainable outcomes, reducing strain on shelters and mental health services.

Responding to the Committee, J. Gordon stressed that while staff and co-creators are resourceful there needs to be full financial investment for the plan to be successful. P. Sweeney confirmed that for the upcoming budget presentation, staff will intentionally break out the upstream investments, such as eviction prevention and rent supplements, to show their proportion of the overall PECH budget. 

Responding to the Committee, C. McEvoy explained that there are three pathways to access affordable housing and rental supplement. The three pathways are: Affordable Housing Waitlist, Prioritized Access to Housing Support, and PECH rental supplements. The pathways eligibility will be determined by staff and staff will help guide individuals towards the most fitting option. He suggested that individuals seeking these pathways ensure that they are on the waitlist. He confirmed that PECH has a specific action to develop an Older Adult Strategy which is meant to address the increase in seniors experiencing homelessness. 

In response to the Committee, J. Gordon agreed that there is a gender disparity related to homelessness and that that addressing the gendered experience of homelessness is a core focus. PECH is working with partners to understand women's hidden homelessness as it relates to extreme weather and safety. The efforts include partnering with the Women's National Housing and Homelessness Network to create service expectation frameworks for all-gender and co-ed spaces, aiming to move beyond service models traditionally informed by male experiences of homelessness.

Responding to the Committee, P. Sweeney confirmed that staff will provide funding information as it relates to how much funding is provided by the Region, the province, and the federal governments. P. Sweeney further confirmed that advocacy for housing and health to be coordinated 

In response to the Committee, P. Sweeney highlighted that staff provide supports for approximately 30-35% individuals from homelessness to permanent housing which is approximately 17 individuals per month. P. Sweeney expressed optimism for the current actions being taken with the growth of chronic homelessness is slowing and those experiencing homelessness is decreasing.

J. Gordon confirmed that PECH staff are actively networking with similar municipalities, particularly in Southern Ontario, to share tools, knowledge, and best practices. The co-creation model used in Waterloo Region, which involves extensive community input, is a point of unique strength, and the goal is to build a system that can withstand drastic provincial trends.

Responding to Committee, P. Sweeney confirmed that the Waterloo Regional Housing Revitalization Plan is rooted in leveraging land the Region already owns. Staff will present an update to Council in November/December during the budget process to offer options on how to accelerate this strategy, including working with non-profits, co-ops, and other housing providers. He noted that approximately half of the 6,000 affordable housing units in the Region are already owned and operated by non-profits and co-ops.

Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-PSV-25-007, Medical Priority Dispatch System (MPDS) Implementation at Cambridge Central Ambulance Communications Centre
notes:
John Riches, Chief and Director of Paramedic Services, provided a presentation on the Medical Priority Dispatch System implementation in Cambridge. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. He identified the current challenges associated with the current system, specifically, that emergency services are being deployed when ambulance care is unnecessary. He provided a comparison between the current and new dispatch models and how the new model has more flexibility based on the priority emergency level. He highlighted that dispatch training and public communication on the change to the model. He confirmed that the new model will be introduced in December 2025. 

Responding to the Committee, J. Riches explained the system used to ask a caller for information about their emergency will be more in depth, however, the process to contact emergency services will be the same. He further explained that the new system is more sophisticated, however, a public communication plan is essential to ensure that the public is properly informed. He confirmed that individuals may exaggerate their symptoms in the current system so he is optimistic that the new model would have more technical questions that will hopefully be able to determine the priority level of the call.

Received for information.

items.title: Other Business
notes:
D. Craig requested an update prior to the end of 2025 on the impact of Heart Hubs and the closure of safe injection sites, including data on overdose deaths and ambulance calls to track improvements in the eviction and overdose crisis. Staff agreed to bring a report back.

D. McCabe asked publicly whether the Region would partner with private sector and non-profit groups to use Region-owned public lands for housing, accelerating construction by letting those organizations own and operate the housing. P. Sweeney confirmed that leveraging Region-owned land is already included in the Housing Revitalization Plan and that staff will present options in the upcoming budget process.
